english: when in Rome, do as the Romans do

terms.comment: Literally “the custom of the place must be observed”. We have found no ancient source for it in Lewis & Short or the loci collections. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
